# Appeal of Denial — Request for Reconsideration

**Cameron Jennings**
[Street address]
[City, State ZIP]
[Phone] | [Email]

**Date:** [Date of this letter]

**To:** Wellpoint — Appeals Department
[Appeal address exactly as printed on my denial letter]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated August 22, 2026**
- **Member:** Cameron Jennings
- **Member ID:** W378650128
- **Reference number:** POC-DA651E8611-76145
- **Service denied:** Total shoulder replacement, CPT 23472
- **Plan:** Wellpoint (Commercial/ACA), State of Georgia
- **Appeal deadline stated in the notice:** February 18, 2027

---

## 1. What I am asking for

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for a total shoulder replacement (CPT 23472), which Wellpoint denied on August 22, 2026 on the ground that the procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity. I am asking Wellpoint to reconsider that decision and approve the procedure.

The criteria listed in the denial come from the **Carelon Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Musculoskeletal — Joint Surgery** (https://guidelines.carelonmedicalbenefitsmanagement.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/PDF-Joint-Surgery-2025-11-15.pdf). Below I set out the plan's own language, quoted exactly, next to what is already in my medical records. My surgeon, Dr. Okafor, MD (orthopedic surgery), has documented that this surgery is needed.

---

## 2. The plan's criteria and what my records show

**The plan's criterion:**

> "Pain and loss of function of at least 6 months' duration that interferes with daily activities (unless radiographs show Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4)"

**My records:** I have had 24 months of progressive shoulder pain that is not relieved by rest. My records document that I cannot reach overhead, cannot dress without help, and cannot sleep on the affected side. That is four times the duration the plan asks for, and the interference with daily activities is described specifically in the chart.

---

**The plan's criterion:**

> "Limited range of motion or crepitus of the glenohumeral joint on physical examination"

**My records:** My examination documents glenohumeral crepitus, active forward elevation limited to 90 degrees, and external rotation limited to 10 degrees. Both halves of this criterion — limited range of motion *and* crepitus — are present and recorded.

---

**The plan's criterion:**

> "*Radiographic evidence of destructive degenerative joint disease as evidenced by marked joint space narrowing AND ONE or more of the following:"

**My records:** My shoulder radiographs of July 21, 2026 (true AP and axillary views) show complete loss of the glenohumeral joint space, together with osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis, and a flattened glenoid. Complete loss of joint space is the most advanced form of the joint space narrowing this criterion describes.

I note that this criterion ends in a colon and introduces a list of further conditions that was not reproduced in the material I received. If Wellpoint is relying on any item from that list, I ask that the reviewer identify in writing which specific item was applied and what in my records was found lacking, so that I can respond to it directly.

---

**The plan's criterion:**

> "Imaging reports obtained within the past 12 months describing the degree of cartilage damage as determined by either or both of the following methods:"

**My records:** My imaging is dated July 21, 2026 — well within twelve months of the request and of this appeal. This criterion also ends in a colon and introduces methods that were not reproduced in what I received; again, I ask Wellpoint to state which method it applied.

---

**The plan's criterion:**

> "Imaging reports should be thorough and describe the presence or absence of subchondral cysts, subchondral sclerosis, periarticular osteophytes, joint subluxation, avascular necrosis , or bone on bone articulations. The degree of joint space narrowing should also be noted."

**My records:** The July 21, 2026 radiograph report describes subchondral sclerosis, osteophytes, a flattened glenoid, and complete loss of the glenohumeral joint space — that is, it notes the degree of joint space narrowing, as the policy asks. A CT was also obtained and confirms an intact rotator cuff. If the reviewer needs the full radiology report to confirm the remaining descriptors, I am enclosing it [enclose complete radiology and CT reports] and my providers can supply anything further on request.

---

**The plan's criteria on conservative care:**

> "Failure of conservative management of at least 6 weeks' duration (unless radiographs show Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 or diffuse modified Outerbridge grade III-IV changes)"

> "Conservative management1 must include a combination of strategies to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and correct underlying dysfunction, including physical therapy AND at least ONE complementary conservative treatment strategy."

> "Patient has completed a full course of conservative management (as defined above) for the current episode of care"

**My records:** I completed supervised physical therapy focused on range of motion and periscapular strengthening — **8 weeks**, from June 6, 2026 to August 1, 2026, **18 visits completed**, documented in the physical therapy discharge note. That exceeds the six weeks the policy specifies. Alongside physical therapy I had two complementary treatments, where the policy requires at least one: NSAIDs for four months with inadequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection on May 31, 2026 that gave only three weeks of partial relief. These measures were aimed at reducing inflammation and relieving pain, and the physical therapy at correcting the underlying dysfunction, which is the combination the policy describes.

---

**The plan's criterion:**

> "Worsening of or no significant improvement in signs and/or symptoms upon clinical reevaluation"

**My records:** After that full course of care, my pain remains progressive and unrelieved by rest, my forward elevation is still limited to 90 degrees and external rotation to 10 degrees, and I still cannot reach overhead, dress without help, or sleep on the affected side. The injection helped for three weeks; the NSAIDs gave inadequate relief. There was no significant improvement.

---

**The plan's criterion:**

> "Clinical notes describing symptom duration and severity, specific functional limitations related to symptoms, and type and duration of all therapeutic measures provided. If conservative management is not appropriate, the reason must be clearly documented."

**My records:** Every element this criterion asks for is in the packet already submitted: duration (24 months) and severity (progressive, unrelieved by rest); specific functional limitations (overhead reach, dressing, sleeping on that side); and the type and duration of each therapeutic measure (18 physical therapy visits over 8 weeks with dates, 4 months of NSAIDs, and a dated corticosteroid injection).

---

**The plan's criteria on suitability for the implant:**

> "Deltoid muscle must be functioning"

> "Shoulder joint must be anatomically and structurally suited to receive selected implants (i.e., adequate bone stock to allow for firm fixation of implant)"

> "Anticipated level of function should place limited demands on the shoulder joint"

**My records:** My records document intact cuff strength on examination and a CT confirming an intact rotator cuff. For the specific findings the plan asks about here, I ask that the following be taken from Dr. Okafor's chart: [deltoid function on examination, as documented by Dr. Okafor]; [bone stock and structural suitability for the selected implant, as documented by Dr. Okafor and on the CT]; and [anticipated postoperative activity level / demands on the shoulder joint, as documented by Dr. Okafor]. If the denial rested on any of these three points, I would ask that Wellpoint say so, because the surgeon's chart speaks to them and they can be supplied promptly.

---

**Criteria that do not apply to my case:** The denial also listed "Proximal humerus fracture confirmed by imaging not amenable to internal fixation (e.g., severe comminution, poor bone quality, multipart, displaced)" and "Malignancy involving the glenohumeral joint or surrounding soft tissue." These are separate pathways in the guideline and are not the basis of my request. My request is made under the pathway the policy describes as "Advanced joint disease of the shoulder due to osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, avascular necrosis (osteonecrosis), or post-traumatic arthritis when ALL the following requirements are met:" — and that heading likewise introduces a list I was not given in full. To the extent Wellpoint applied a requirement from that list that I have not addressed above, I ask that it be identified.

---

## 3. Why I am asking for reconsideration

The denial notice tells me only that the procedure "does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity." It does not tell me which criterion was not met or what evidence was found missing. When I compare the plan's published criteria to my records point by point, the documentation appears to be present: the duration requirement is met several times over, the conservative-care requirement is exceeded, the examination findings and current imaging are on file, and my surgeon has documented that this procedure is needed.

I also want to note plainly that I have quoted only the guideline language that was provided to me. I have not stated any threshold, grade, or requirement that does not appear in that language, and where the policy text I have ends in a colon, I have not guessed at the list that follows.

---

## 4. What I am requesting

1. That Wellpoint overturn the August 22, 2026 denial (reference POC-DA651E8611-76145) and authorize CPT 23472.
2. That the appeal be reviewed by a physician reviewer with experience in orthopedic shoulder surgery.
3. That, if the denial is maintained, Wellpoint identify in writing the specific criterion from the Carelon Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Musculoskeletal — Joint Surgery that was not met and the specific evidence considered lacking, along with information about my further appeal rights, including external review.

I am submitting this appeal within the timeframe stated in my denial notice, which gives a deadline of **February 18, 2027**. I am sending it to the appeal address printed on that notice. If there is any additional step you need me to take to have this appeal accepted and reviewed, please let me know and I will take it promptly.

Thank you for taking a fresh look at this. I am glad to provide any additional records, and Dr. Okafor's office can be reached to discuss the clinical details directly.

**Enclosures:** copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-22; physical therapy discharge note (18 visits, 06/06/2026–08/01/2026); radiology report dated 07/21/2026; CT report; office/operative planning notes from Dr. Okafor; [any other records you are enclosing]

---

Sincerely,

**Cameron Jennings**
Member ID: W378650128
[Signature]
[Date]

[Phone] | [Email]
[Mailing address]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
